info.title: Stogas Gateway API
info.description: OpenAI-compatible API for every catalog model. Authenticate with your API key, and the gateway sends the request to the provider that your policies select.

servers.description: Gateway origin. Endpoint paths include their API version.

get.description: Returns the root of the active public catalog: the places that data handling names, authors, groups and providers in full, a summary of each model, route and deployment, the scheduled changes to them, and the parts that hold models, routes and deployments in full. The root keeps each retired record, and each record gives its retirement date.

200.description: Root of the active public catalog, with the sequence and digest of its release.

get.description: Returns a part that the active catalog's root names: models, routes and deployments in full, with their prices and scheduled changes. `/v1/catalog` names each part by SHA-256, and a part's bytes never change.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description: SHA-256 of the part in hex, as `/v1/catalog` names it.

200.description: The part, whose bytes have the SHA-256 in the path.

404.description: The active catalog names no part with this SHA-256, as when a newer catalog has replaced it, or each record in the part had retired when the gateway loaded the catalog. Read `/v1/catalog` again.

get.description: Lists the IDs that the `model` field accepts, in the OpenAI format.

post.description: Creates a chat completion. The gateway checks each field against the selected deployment before it calls the provider.

200.description: Successful completion. Non-streaming requests return JSON; streaming requests return Server-Sent Events.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each `data:` frame contains a chat completion chunk. When a receipt is requested, a `: stogas {...}` comment appears before `data: [DONE]`. SSE clients ignore the comment.

post.description: Creates a model response. The gateway checks each field against the selected deployment before it calls the provider.

200.description: Successful response. Non-streaming requests return JSON; streaming requests return Server-Sent Events.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each `data:` frame contains a Responses API event. When a receipt is requested, a `: stogas {...}` comment appears before `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`. SSE clients ignore the comment.

post.description: Checks the policies that would apply to a request, without saving them or calling a model. A member can check with a grant from `POST /api/{orgId}/policies/check-grant` instead of an API key, such as for a plugin's settings before encrypting them.

policySources.description: Exactly one organization and one key policy, plus each folder, grant, member and credential policy that applies, and up to 30 role policies. Each entry has its scope, its `id` where the scope has one, and its policy object or `null`.

encryption_keys.description: Encryption keys by label, as unpadded base64url. Send the keys of encrypted exports and redactions to check them too. The gateway never stores or logs them.

status.description: `valid` when every policy was checked. `partial` when an encrypted plugin's key was not sent, so that plugin was not checked.

rule.description: The rule that holds the plugin, when the policy's own settings do not.

plugin.description: The encrypted plugin that was not checked.

uncheckedPlugins.description: Each encrypted plugin that was not checked, with its policy and rule.

400.description: The policies are invalid (`invalid_policy`), or an encryption key is missing or wrong. Without `encryption_keys`, an `invalid_policy` message says what is wrong; with them, it does not, since it could repeat encrypted settings. See [400 errors](/docs/reference/errors#400-bad-request).

post.description: Checks a customer-encrypted credential with the same free provider call as Check credential on the dashboard, and saves the result on the credential. An Azure credential's check also discovers the deployments of its account, which become its targets. Authenticate with a grant from `POST /api/{orgId}/byok/{byokId}/check-grant`, and send the request through a verified connection, as `stogas byok check` does.

encryption_keys.description: Encryption keys by registered label, as unpadded base64url, with the key that encrypted the credential under the grant's `keyLabel`. The gateway never stores or logs them.

200.description: The provider answered, or could not be reached, and the result is saved.

checkError.description: `null` when the provider accepted the credential, and otherwise why it did not, as the dashboard shows it.

selected.description: The selected targets, at most one for each model.

unavailable.description: The selected targets that cannot serve now, such as a deleted deployment.

unselected.description: The models that have a target that can serve but none selected.

azureTargets.description: For an Azure credential, its targets after the check, which discovers the account's deployments, counted as the dashboard counts them. `null` for other providers.

400.description: The body holds more than `encryption_keys` (`invalid_request`), a key is missing or wrong (`encryption_key_required`), the organization no longer registers the credential's key (`byok_key_unregistered`), or the credential is stored by Stogas (`credential_stored`). See [400 errors](/docs/reference/errors#400-bad-request).

401.description: The grant is missing, invalid or expired (`invalid_check_grant`).

error.message: The credential check grant is invalid or expired. Run the check again.

403.description: You no longer manage the credential (`permission_denied`), or the organization is inactive (`organization_inactive`). See [403 errors](/docs/reference/errors#403-forbidden).

404.description: The credential was deleted, or you left its organization (`credential_not_found`).

409.description: The credential changed, or another check finished, during this check (`credential_changed`). Check it again.

bearerAuth.description: Send the API key as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`.

apiKeyHeader.name: api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: Also accepted: `api-key: <api_key>`, for SDKs that send it.

xApiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
xApiKeyHeader.description: Also accepted: `x-api-key: <api_key>`, for SDKs that send it.

xGoogApiKeyHeader.name: x-goog-api-key
xGoogApiKeyHeader.description: Also accepted: `x-goog-api-key: <api_key>`, for SDKs that send it.

checkGrant.description: Send the grant from `POST /api/{orgId}/byok/{byokId}/check-grant` as `Authorization: Bearer <grant>`. It lets you check that one credential for five minutes.

policyCheckGrant.description: Send the grant from `POST /api/{orgId}/policies/check-grant` as `Authorization: Bearer <grant>`. For five minutes, it lets you check policies for that organization.

Metadata.name: Stogas-Metadata
Metadata.description: Set to `v2` to add the `stogas` object, with usage, cost, a signed [receipt](/docs/receipts) and its salts, to the response.

SessionId.name: X-Session-Id
SessionId.description: Groups the request with others in the same [session](/docs/request-records#sessions). Send it at most once. The body's `session_id` takes precedence.

BadRequest.description: The request is invalid, or the selected deployment cannot accept it. See [400 errors](/docs/reference/errors#400-bad-request).

error.message: Invalid text completion request: the 'messages' array cannot be empty.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing, wrong or deleted.

PaymentRequired.description: The organization needs more credit, or a spending limit is reached. See [402 errors](/docs/reference/errors#402-payment-required).

error.message: Insufficient credit. Add funds to your organization to retry this request.

Forbidden.description: The key or a policy scope is disabled or expired, or a deny period blocks requests now. See [403 errors](/docs/reference/errors#403-forbidden).

RequestTimeout.description: The request body took longer than five minutes to arrive. See [408 errors](/docs/reference/errors#404-405-408-and-415).

error.message: The request body did not arrive within 5 minutes.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is above 128 MiB after decompression, or above another request limit. See [413 errors](/docs/reference/errors#413-content-too-large).

error.message: Decompressed request body exceeds max allowed size of 134217728 bytes

RateLimited.description: A request, token or concurrency limit is reached. Wait for `Retry-After` when it is present. See [429 errors](/docs/reference/errors#429-too-many-requests).

InternalError.description: The gateway could not complete the request. See [500 errors](/docs/reference/errors#500-internal-server-error).

CatalogUnavailable.description: The gateway has no approved catalog loaded.

FailedDependency.description: The provider credential or account behind the deployment failed the request. A retry fails until it changes. See [424 errors](/docs/reference/errors#424-failed-dependency).

error.message: The configured provider credential was rejected

BadGateway.description: A provider call failed after the gateway sent the request, so the provider may have run it, or the provider sent an invalid response. See [502 errors](/docs/reference/errors#502-bad-gateway).

error.message: Provider attempt 1 (deployment openai-gpt-5.6-sol) failed after the gateway sent the request, so the provider may have run it. Send the request again only if a second run is acceptable.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The gateway or the provider is temporarily unavailable. Send the request again later. See [503 errors](/docs/reference/errors#503-service-unavailable).

error.message: The gateway is temporarily unavailable. Retry the request later.

GatewayTimeout.description: A [timeout](/docs/policies/timeouts) expired, or a provider call timed out after the gateway sent the request. See [504 errors](/docs/reference/errors#504-gateway-timeout).

error.message: The response timed out. Generation may continue and be billed.

sequence.description: The release's sequence number, which grows with each release.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the root that the release signs: this response without `sequence` and `digest`.

locations.description: The places that records name, by ID: `world`; continents, such as `europe`; regions, such as `apac`; unions, such as `eu`; countries, by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; and subdivisions, by ISO 3166-2 code. A continent, region or union lists every country that it covers, and every place but `world` lists the places that directly contain it: a country lies in each smallest region that lists it, a region in each smallest region that lists all of its countries, and a subdivision in its country. A deployment's `processingLocation` and `storageLocation` are places, `unknown`, or, for storage only, `none`.

countries.description: Continents, regions and unions only: every country that the place covers, by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code and in order, including countries that the catalog does not list.

description.description: What the place covers, when its name does not say.

kind.description: What kind of place it is.

parts.description: The parts that hold models, routes and deployments in full. Parts hold the records without a retirement date first and then the others by date, and the records that Stogas does not serve last, in parts of their own. Fetch each from `/v1/catalog/parts/{sha256}`, and check that its bytes have this SHA-256 and size.

through.description: The latest retirement date of a record in the part, or `null` when a record in it has none. Every record in the part has retired once this date has.

stogasSupported.description: Whether Stogas serves the records in the part. The gateway never reads a part that Stogas does not serve, and a reader that shows only what Stogas serves can skip it.

periods.description: The named periods that make the dated states.

end.description: `null` when the period has no end.

schedule.description: Dated catalog states, oldest first. Each state lasts until the next one starts. Its `summaries` lists in full every author, group and provider that differs from `summaries` during it, and the summary of each model, route and deployment whose summary differs. Each part lists its records that differ during the state in full, under the same `start`.

summaries.description: Every record of the catalog, current or retired, by kind and ID. Authors, groups and providers are whole; the part that a summary names holds its model, route or deployment in full.

CatalogRetirementDate.description: The date on which the record retires, or `null` while there is none. The provider can name one for a deployment, a route or itself, and can mean the start or the end of the date in any time zone, so the gateway serves the record until the date has ended everywhere, at 12:00 UTC on the next day. A provider's date ends each of its routes, and a deployment retires once its routes have all retired. Any record retires with the last of the records it exists for, once all of them have dates: a model or a route with its deployments, a provider with its routes, an author with its models and a group with the models in it.

CatalogModelSummary.description: What the root says of a model. Its part holds the rest.

part.description: Index in `parts` of the part that holds the record.

CatalogRouteSummary.description: What the root says of a route. Its part holds the rest.

part.description: Index in `parts` of the part that holds the record.

CatalogDeploymentSummary.description: What the root says of a deployment. Its part holds the rest.

part.description: Index in `parts` of the part that holds the record.

routeIds.description: IDs of the deployment's routes, sorted.

CatalogPartResponse.description: A part: models, routes and deployments in full, with their changes in each dated state.

graph.description: The part's records in full, by kind and ID: models, routes, and deployments with their routes, prices, limits, data handling and notes.

schedule.description: The dated states in which records of this part differ from `graph`, oldest first. Each lists in full the records that differ during it, and starts at a `start` of the root's `schedule`.

id.description: A model ID, alias or deployment ID, or a group in the form `group:claude`.

created.description: The release date of the model that the ID names, as a Unix time. A group shows its newest model's.

owned_by.description: The author of the model that the ID names. A group shows its newest model's.

message.description: A description for people. The text can change.

code.description: A stable code for handling the error. Every gateway error has one; a provider error can have `null`. See [Errors](/docs/reference/errors).

param.description: The request field related to the error, when known.

oneOf.description: One provider ID, such as `openai` or `anthropic`.
oneOf.title: Provider ID

only.description: Providers that can serve the request.

order.description: Providers to try first, in order.

ProviderRoutingPreference.description: Providers to allow or prefer for this request. The gateway removes it before it calls the provider. See [Choose a model](/docs/models#choose-a-model).

ChatCompletionRequest.description: Request body. An unknown top-level field returns `400` with the field in `param`; `null` counts as omitted. See [Compatibility notes](/docs/reference/provider-behavior).

model.description: A model ID, alias or deployment ID, or terms such as `group:gpt-6` or `provider:azure gpt-5.6-sol` that select a group or also choose where the request runs. Omit it to let your [routing policy](/docs/policies/routing) choose. See [Models](/docs/models).

provider.description: Providers to allow or prefer for this request. The gateway removes it before it calls the provider. See [Choose a model](/docs/models#choose-a-model).

messages.description: The conversation. Each assistant tool call needs its tool result in the same request.

store.description: Only `false` is accepted. The gateway never asks a provider to store a response.

frequency_penalty.description: Lowers the chance of repeating tokens by how often they appear. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

logit_bias.description: Raises or lowers the chance of specific token IDs. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

logprobs.description: Return the log probability of each output token. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

max_completion_tokens.description: The most output tokens, including reasoning. Each deployment sets its own maximum.

metadata.description: Labels that the request record keeps for analytics filters, downloads and exports. Up to 16 pairs: keys have 1 to 64 bytes and values up to 512 bytes in UTF-8, without control characters. The gateway does not send metadata to the provider.

session_id.description: Groups the request with others in the same [session](/docs/request-records#sessions), which analytics can filter by. Up to 256 bytes in UTF-8, without control characters. Takes precedence over the `X-Session-Id` header. The gateway does not send it to the provider.

n.description: Number of choices. Only `1` is accepted.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model can call several tools at once.

prediction.description: Expected output, which lets some OpenAI models respond faster.

presence_penalty.description: Lowers the chance of repeating tokens that already appear. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

repetition_penalty.description: Penalizes tokens that already appear, where `1` means no penalty. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

prompt_cache_key.description: Groups requests that share a prompt prefix, up to 256 bytes. Not every provider accepts it; see [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

prompt_cache_retention.description: How long the provider keeps the cache. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

prompt_cache_options.description: Choose automatic caching or explicit breakpoints. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

cache_control.description: Anthropic prompt caching: `{"type": "ephemeral"}` with an optional `ttl` of `5m` or `1h`. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

enabled.description: `true` turns reasoning on at the level nearest to `medium`. `false` turns it off.

effort.description: How much the model reasons. Each deployment lists the levels it accepts as `reasoningEfforts` in the [catalog](/docs/reasoning#check-a-deployment), and the gateway sends the nearest one. `none` fails when the model cannot turn reasoning off.

max_tokens.description: The most reasoning tokens. Each deployment sets its own range.

mode.description: `pro` selects the model's [Pro deployment](/docs/reasoning#select-pro-mode), and `standard` its standard deployment.

reasoning_effort.description: Another name for `reasoning.effort`. Send only one.

reasoning_max_tokens.description: Another name for `reasoning.max_tokens`. Send only one.

response_format.description: Ask for JSON, or JSON that matches a schema. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

seed.description: Asks the provider to sample the same way each time. Results can still differ.

service_tier.description: The service tier. A model that your key can use only at other tiers returns `service_tier_unavailable`. See [Service tiers](/docs/service-tiers).

stream_options.description: Requires `stream: true`. Usage is always included, so `include_usage` is always `true`.

stop.description: A string, or a list of strings, that ends the output.

stop_sequences.description: Anthropic name for stop sequences. Send `stop` or `stop_sequences`, not both.

temperature.description: Passed to the provider as is. The provider decides which values its model accepts.

top_logprobs.description: How many likely tokens to return at each position. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

top_k.description: Sample from the K most likely tokens. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

top_p.description: Passed to the provider as is. The provider decides which values its model accepts.

safety_identifier.description: An opaque ID for your end user, such as a hash of your user ID, so the provider can act on that user instead of your whole account. Your own OpenAI and Azure OpenAI credentials receive it as sent, and Anthropic models receive it as `metadata.user_id`. The gateway removes it for Chutes and with a Stogas-managed credential.

user.description: The older name for an end-user ID. Your own OpenAI and Azure OpenAI credentials receive it when it has at most 64 characters, and Anthropic models receive it as `metadata.user_id` when `safety_identifier` is absent. The gateway removes it for Chutes and with a Stogas-managed credential.

verbosity.description: How long the answer is: `low`, `medium` or `high`. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

web_search_options.description: Search settings for search models such as `gpt-5-search-api`. See [OpenAI](/docs/providers/openai#tools).

encryption_keys.description: Encryption keys by registered label, as unpadded base64url, for [encrypted policies](/docs/customer-encryption). The gateway removes them before it calls the provider and never stores or logs them.

messages.content: Reflect on the issue of trusting trust

object.description: The object type, which is always "chat.completion"

model.description: The ID of the model that served the request, such as `gpt-5.6-sol`. See [Models](/docs/models#choose-a-model).

message.content: You can never fully trust code you did not write yourself.

ChatMessage.description: A message. Images, files and audio go only in user messages.

tool_call_id.description: Tool call ID for tool response messages.

refusal.description: Assistant refusal text when provided by the model.

reasoning.description: Reasoning text, when the model returns it.

reasoning_content.description: Another name for `reasoning`. A reply carries the text under both names. A request takes either one, or both when they are equal.

reasoning_details.description: Reasoning from an earlier reply. Send it back unchanged. Anthropic-format deployments take it, and so do OpenAI deployments, which get the request [through Responses](/docs/providers#chat-completions-through-responses).

finish_reason.description: Reason why the model stopped generating

ChatUsage.description: Token usage. Prices and meters are in the [`stogas` object](/docs/receipts).

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the prompt

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the completion

ChatMessageContent.description: Message content as either a string or an array of content blocks.

index.description: The call's position in a reply. You can send it back, and no provider receives it.

arguments.description: A string that encodes a JSON object.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls made by the assistant

prompt_cache_breakpoint.description: Marks the end of a cached prefix when `prompt_cache_options` is explicit.

cache_control.description: Anthropic prompt caching for this block. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

ResponsesRequest.description: Request body. An unknown top-level field returns `400` with the field in `param`; `null` counts as omitted. See [Compatibility notes](/docs/reference/provider-behavior).

model.description: A model ID, alias or deployment ID, or terms such as `group:gpt-6` or `provider:azure gpt-5.6-sol` that select a group or also choose where the request runs. Omit it to let your [routing policy](/docs/policies/routing) choose. See [Models](/docs/models).

provider.description: Providers to allow or prefer for this request. The gateway removes it before it calls the provider. See [Choose a model](/docs/models#choose-a-model).

input.description: A string, or a list of input items. Each tool call needs its output in the same list.

store.description: Only `false` is accepted. The gateway never asks a provider to store a response.

include.description: Extra output to return, such as `reasoning.encrypted_content`. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

instructions.description: A system message that comes before `input`.

max_output_tokens.description: The most output tokens, including reasoning. Each deployment sets its own maximum.

max_tool_calls.description: The most hosted tool calls, such as web searches, in the request, from 1 to 128. It needs a hosted tool. Without it, the hold covers ten calls and the model decides how many it makes. See [Hosted tools](/docs/model-tools#hosted-tools).

metadata.description: Labels that the request record keeps for analytics filters, downloads and exports. Up to 16 pairs: keys have 1 to 64 bytes and values up to 512 bytes in UTF-8, without control characters. The gateway does not send metadata to the provider.

session_id.description: Groups the request with others in the same [session](/docs/request-records#sessions), which analytics can filter by. Up to 256 bytes in UTF-8, without control characters. Takes precedence over the `X-Session-Id` header. The gateway does not send it to the provider.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model can call several tools at once.

prompt_cache_key.description: Groups requests that share a prompt prefix, up to 256 bytes. Not every provider accepts it; see [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

prompt_cache_retention.description: How long the provider keeps the cache. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

max_tokens.description: The most reasoning tokens. Each deployment sets its own range.

mode.description: `pro` selects the model's [Pro deployment](/docs/reasoning#select-pro-mode), and `standard` its standard deployment.

service_tier.description: The service tier. A model that your key can use only at other tiers returns `service_tier_unavailable`. See [Service tiers](/docs/service-tiers).

stream_options.description: Requires `stream: true`. Usage is always included.

temperature.description: Passed to the provider as is. The provider decides which values its model accepts.

frequency_penalty.description: Lowers the chance of repeating tokens by how often they appear. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

presence_penalty.description: Lowers the chance of repeating tokens that already appear. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

format.description: Plain text, JSON, or JSON that matches a schema. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

top_logprobs.description: How many likely tokens to return at each position. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

top_k.description: Sample from the K most likely tokens. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

top_p.description: Passed to the provider as is. The provider decides which values its model accepts.

tool_choice.description: `auto`, `none`, `required`, one named tool, or `allowed_tools`. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

tools.description: Functions, custom tools, web search and web fetch. See [Tools](/docs/model-tools).

truncation.description: What the provider does with input longer than the context window. Not every provider accepts it; see [Providers](/docs/providers).

access_programs.description: OpenAI's cyber access program for this request. OpenAI deployments only: another provider returns `400` for a selected program. Without it, OpenAI picks the program from the model and your project's access. Daybreak programs need OpenAI's approval for the project of your own OpenAI credential.

client_metadata.description: Client details that Codex sends with each request. The gateway accepts them and never sends them to the provider.

prompt_cache_options.description: Choose automatic caching or explicit breakpoints. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

stop_sequences.description: Anthropic name for stop sequences. Send `stop` or `stop_sequences`, not both.

cache_control.description: Anthropic prompt caching: `{"type": "ephemeral"}` with an optional `ttl` of `5m` or `1h`. See [Prompt caching](/docs/prompt-caching).

reasoning.effort.description: Another name for `reasoning.effort`. Send only one.

id.description: Response ID, set by the gateway.

object.description: The object type, which is always `response`.

model.description: The ID of the model that served the request, such as `gpt-5.6-sol`. See [Models](/docs/models#choose-a-model).

output_text.description: All output text joined, when there is any.

content.text: You can never fully trust code you did not write yourself.

example.output_text: You can never fully trust code you did not write yourself.

ResponsesInputItem.description: An output item: a message, a tool call, reasoning or a hosted tool result.

output.description: Tool output payload for function_call_output and related output items.

ResponsesUsage.description: Token usage. Prices and meters are in the [`stogas` object](/docs/receipts).

ResponsesMessageContent.description: Responses message content as either a string or an array of content blocks.

ResponsesRequestInputItem.description: An input item: a message, a tool call, a tool output or reasoning from an earlier response.

phase.description: The label that OpenAI gives each assistant message of a reply. You can send it back.

arguments.description: Function arguments encoded as a JSON object string.

ResponsesRequestMessageContent.description: Text, or a list of content blocks. See [Images and files](/docs/input-files).

AnthropicTaskBudget.description: Anthropic only. See [Anthropic request fields](/docs/providers/anthropic#anthropic-request-fields). It guides the model and does not lower the hold.

PromptTokenDetails.description: Input token details. `cached_tokens` were read from the cache, and `cache_write_tokens` were written to it.

created_at.description: When the gateway handled the request, by its own clock.

ttft_ms.description: Time to the first generated token in a stream.

provider.description: Provider details, such as the provider request ID. The receipt covers them.

salts.description: The random salt that each commitment covers. Only you receive them: share a side's salt to prove that side. Request records and exports don't have them.

usd.description: Exact USD amount as a decimal string.

rateUsd.description: Exact USD amount as a decimal string.

upstream_cost_usd.description: Exact USD amount as a decimal string.

boot_sha256.description: The boot record whose key signed the receipt.

RequestPolicy.description: Optional request policy, at most 16 KiB. Requires saved delegation.request permission. Required settings intersect saved policies; defaults can be replaced. Shared limits and delegation are forbidden. Consumed by the gateway and never forwarded upstream.

totalSeconds.description: Longest total wait, from when the gateway admits the request body. Defaults to 3600. Credential policies, and rules whose condition reads author, model, deployment, route or provider fields, cannot set it.

outputIdleSeconds.description: Longest wait for useful provider output, from each provider call and after each output. Defaults to 3600, so only totalSeconds applies. Each call uses the value for its own deployment and credential.

timeouts.description: For each timeout, the smallest required value applies. A timeout ends your wait, but provider work that has started continues and is billed.

end.description: The end must be later than the start. Split an overnight period into two entries.

timeZone.description: UTC or an IANA time zone name with its exact capitalization, such as America/New_York.

access.description: Weekly periods when the gateway refuses requests.

asciiOnly.description: Reject non-ASCII decoded text in redaction-scanned input fields before redaction. Any parent requirement wins.

allow.description: Admit only attachments of these types. An empty list admits none. Allow lists of several policies intersect.

deny.description: Refuse attachments of these types. Deny lists of several policies join.

mediaTypes.description: Limit attachments by media type, such as `image/png`, or class, such as `image/*`. The gateway checks an inline attachment's declared type against the start of its content, and refuses a URL or file ID wherever its type could decide.

input.description: Checks on request input before redaction.

url.description: Complete JSON webhook URL. No path is appended.

headers.description: Destination authentication headers. Encrypt the export to keep them private when saved.

content.description: Send request and response bodies. Defaults to true, and false sends the request record and metadata only.

destinations.description: Independent destinations from required policies are combined. Destinations with the same URL and headers are sent once, with bodies if any of them sends bodies. At most eight combined destinations. An empty array adds none and replaces plugin defaults.

anyOf.description: These settings, encrypted with `stogas encrypt`. The gateway reads them only with the encryption key a request sends.

textExtraction.description: Turn inline UTF-8 text files into prompt text before input checks and redaction. `auto`, which applies when no policy sets a mode, keeps a file that the deployment reads as a file unless input checks or redaction must read it, and `always` turns every one into text. The strongest required mode applies.

customPattern.description: One RE2 expression, limited to 512 UTF-8 bytes.

items.description: Exact text, up to 256 UTF-8 bytes. Not a regular expression.

values.description: Plain text strings, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. Settings apply to every value.

fuzzy.description: Allow one ASCII insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent swap

literals.description: Groups of literal strings sharing case, boundary and fuzzy settings. At most 1,000 strings and 65,536 UTF-8 text bytes in total.

anyOf.description: An empty object adds no redaction and replaces redaction defaults. Required redaction from other policies still applies.
These settings, encrypted with `stogas encrypt`. The gateway reads them only with the encryption key a request sends.

plugins.description: Text extraction, redaction and export of each request and response to your webhook. Encrypt the export or the redaction to keep its settings private.

allowedCatalogNodes.description: A candidate must match each list that is present. Lists share the policy byte budget. An empty object replaces default lists without removing other required lists.

retries.description: Calls to the same deployment and credential after a call that the provider did not run: a 409 or 429 response, or a connection that failed before the provider received the request, unless the provider's x-should-retry header says otherwise. Defaults to 0. The smallest value that applies wins.

fallbacks.description: Other deployment and credential pairs to try, in routing order, after a pair fails without running the request. Defaults to 2. The smallest value that applies wins. Credential policies, and rules whose condition reads author, model, deployment, route or provider fields, cannot set it.

missingEncryptionKeys.description: What happens when a deployment and credential pair needs an encryption key that the request didn't send. fail, the default, fails the request. skip leaves out only that pair, so the request can use its other pairs. fail wins when policies differ.

filter.description: A CEL filter over catalog facts, request model, route and time. Input-token and cost estimates are unavailable during routing.

by.description: A CEL expression over author, model, deployment, route or provider fields, such as blended_price(3, 1). random() or random(weight), without a direction, gives a weighted random order and must come last.

direction.description: Defaults to asc. Missing values sort last in either direction. Lists take none.

authors.description: Author IDs in the order to try. Candidates not listed come last.

models.description: Model IDs in the order to try. Candidates not listed come last.

deployments.description: Deployment IDs in the order to try. Candidates not listed come last.

routes.description: Route IDs in the order to try. Candidates not listed come last.

providers.description: Provider IDs in the order to try. Candidates not listed come last.

sort.description: Up to four criteria that order the deployments a request can use. Each orders the ties of the one before. A criterion is by, a CEL expression with an optional direction, or one list of author, model, deployment, route or provider IDs, which ranks candidates by their position in the list. Required criteria apply from the organization policy down to the request policy, then default criteria from the closest policy out. A request fails, naming the tied models or deployments, when the criteria leave a tie among those it would try.

routing.description: Which deployments and credentials requests may use and in which order, and how often a request retries or falls back.

rules.description: Unordered named rules. Names identify conditional counters and never give precedence.

CatalogStogasSupported.description: Whether Stogas serves the record. The catalog lists the whole market, so it also lists what Stogas does not serve, and the record's `notes` say why. A provider that Stogas does not serve passes that to its routes, and a route to its deployments. A model, provider, author or group goes unserved once Stogas serves none of its deployments, routes or models. A request that names only records that Stogas does not serve fails with `model_unavailable`.
